key_insight: Oxygen content controls oxychloride framework connectivity, with fast Li-ion transport favored by low-dimensional frameworks that enable three-dimensional migration through low-barrier, energetically similar Li sites.
engineering_relevance: Tuning the oxygen-to-chlorine ratio offers a design route to lithium oxyhalide solid electrolytes with high predicted room-temperature Li mobility.
method: Crystal structure prediction across Nb-, Ta-, Ti-, Zr-, and Hf-based oxychlorides.
Molecular dynamics using machine-learning interatomic potentials.
Migration analysis using potential-of-mean-force maps and nudged elastic band calculations.
evidence_signal: Simulations find fast Li diffusion in Group 5 compositions at oxygen contents x ≈ 0.67–1.5 and identify four stable Nb/Ta candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities up to ~10⁻⁶ cm²/s.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational predictions; experimental synthesis, ionic conductivity, and device compatibility remain to be validated.
paper_title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
